plan: The dominant strategy in this auction is to bid your value. This is because, if you bid less than your value, you risk losing the item to someone who values it more, and you miss out on potential profit. If you bid more than your value, you risk overpaying and losing money. Since this is round 1 of 1, and there's no history to learn from, I will strictly adhere to the dominant strategy. My value is $9, so I will bid $9.

The dominant strategy in this second-price sealed-bid auction is to bid your true value. This is because you win if and only if your bid is the highest, and your payoff is your value minus the second-highest bid. Bidding less than your value risks losing the auction even when the prize is worth more than the second-highest bid. Bidding more than your value risks winning the auction and paying more than the prize is worth. Therefore, I will bid my value of $40.

The dominant strategy in this all-pay auction is to bid your value. While collusion could be profitable, it's impossible to coordinate with other bidders. Since this is the only round, and my value is $32, I will bid my value. This maximizes my expected profit, as I win when my value is higher than the second-highest bid and pay only the second-highest bid if I win.
